title: Django Dos Chili (Django Dos F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Django Dos chili is an F1 hybrid chili variety from East West Seed. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Django Dos chili is an F1 hybrid chili variety, also sold or known as Django Dos F1 or Django 2. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from East West Seed.

heroImage.alt: A farmer watering vegetable beds in Pulilan, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Django Dos chili is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Django Dos F1 or Django 2, this is the same chili. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [chili variety finder](/crop-varieties/chili), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation).
Key facts about Django Dos chili

blocks.caption: From its seller and farm sources

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit chili fields most often: [tomato leaf curl](/diseases/tomato-leaf-curl), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Glossy light green, even sized and mildly hot.
Rated intermediate against cucumber mosaic virus.
Packs state 97 percent hybridity and 85 percent germination or better.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: sold in Philippine online farm shops beside Django, one of the ten best selling East West seeds at Baliuag Marketing. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual chili on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Django Dos chili

Decide first between siling haba, the long green finger chili for cooking, and siling labuyo, the small hot one. Hybrids bear more and for longer, while open pollinated labuyo keeps its heat and lets you save seed. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.

items.q: Is Django Dos F1 the same as Django Dos?
items.a: Yes. Django Dos F1 is another name for Django Dos. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Django Dos?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
